about:
Design Warehouse has operated as a Santa Fe, New Mexico institution since 1981. The retailer maintains hours Monday through Saturday and offers validated parking for visitors at its Lincoln Avenue location.

The business curates a selection of furniture, lamps, and home accessories for residential customers. Its showroom presents bedroom settings, couch and coffee table displays, dining room tables, and desks. The product assortment includes lines such as the Garden Party Wardrobe System in Oblivion and White finishes. Orders are fulfilled through USPS for smaller items and common carrier for furniture, with all web and furniture sales marked final. Shipping costs are tiered by order value, with free shipping on orders over $100.

The store serves individual consumers rather than industrial or commercial buyers. Local Flavor Magazine has described it as the place in town for artfully designed home furnishings, noting elegant bedroom settings and sleek contemporary displays.

The company emphasizes personal service, stating a preference for phone communication and providing direct contact for shipping quotes to 47 states.

name: Detroit Woodworking
old_description: Detroit Woodworking specializes in custom residential woodworking, collaborating with homeowners, architects, and designers to create handcrafted cabinetry, intricate moldings, and custom furniture with exceptional attention to detail. Serving Grosse Pointe and Metro Detroit, we blend traditional and modern design using premium materials to craft durable, inviting spaces while ensuring a seamless experience from consultation to installation.
about:
Detroit Woodworking operates a design-build custom millwork shop in Roseville, Michigan. The family-owned business serves metro Detroit and ships nationwide, drawing on decades of experience in millwork and cabinetry.

The company produces custom cabinetry, architectural millwork, custom doors, live-edge furniture, conference tables, healthcare and educational casework, and specialty fabrication including prototype and one-off pieces. Its production facility combines CNC machining, laser engraving, and professional finishing systems with traditional craftsmanship. The shop handles projects from design engineering through installation, using AutoCAD drawings and 3D renderings to develop each job.

Clients include homeowners, architects, designers, developers, and corporations across residential construction, hospitality, restaurants, retail, healthcare, education, multi-family, and corporate environments. The firm has delivered custom cabinetry, fixtures, and displays for local businesses and large-scale replicable millwork programs.

Detroit Woodworking emphasizes a seamless experience from consultation to installation, offering dedicated project management, white-glove delivery, climate-controlled storage, and a limited lifetime warranty on all custom cabinetry and millwork. The shop notes it is one of the few in the Detroit area with a state-of-the-art laser engraving machine for intricate detailing.

name: Diabetic Equipment And Supplies
old_description: Regardless of whether you live with Type 1 Diabetes or Type 2 Diabetes one thing remains…when you don’t have your supplies it is stressful and can be dangerous. We understand the critical nature of insulin pumps, CGMs and glucometers and it impacts everything we do.
about:
Diabetic Equipment and Supplies (DES) operates from Johnston, Iowa, with an additional location in Indiana, serving customers across 26 states. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

DES distributes diabetes management equipment, including insulin pumps, continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), and glucometers. The company assigns each patient a dedicated Patient Care Coordinator who handles the entire ordering process, works with Medicaid, Medicare, and commercial insurance plans, and manages recurring resupply shipments with no shipping fees. Coordinators specialize exclusively in diabetes products and insurance navigation.

The company serves individuals with Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes, as well as endocrinologists, healthcare providers, diabetes educators, and other medical professionals. Its service area spans 26 states, with outreach conducted via phone, text, and email for resupply reminders and personal follow-up.

DES emphasizes a relationship-based model: calls are answered by a live person without phone trees, and coordinators proactively contact patients when supplies are due. The firm states that its staff works with diabetes products 100% of the time, positioning them as specialists in both product selection and insurance coordination.

name: Dickson Industries Inc
old_description: Since 1946, the Dickson name has guaranteed integrity, innovation, and a commitment to excellence. Generations of customers have relied on Dickson to deliver on our promise.
about:
Dickson Industries Inc. traces its roots to April 30, 1946, when Allied Manufacturing Co. was founded at 115 SW 8th Street in Des Moines, Iowa. The company began producing cotton stockinette for meat packers and food processors. Arthur D. Dickson, initially hired as a sales engineer, purchased the business in the 1960s and renamed it Dickson Industries, Inc., moving operations to the Interstate Bakery Building at 325 SW 5th Street. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the company is led by President David Dickson, grandson of the founder.

Today Dickson operates a 50,000-square-foot facility in Des Moines with 49 employees and 216 knitting machines, offering complete cut-and-sew operations and in-house embroidery through its Dickson Designs division. The company produces a range of knit fabrics, garments, and textile products, including custom-designed casings, stockinette, medical fabrics, lab and butcher coats, insulated garments, and filtration fabrics. All products are researched, tested, and manufactured to customer specifications, with proprietary information kept confidential.

Dickson serves food processing (DeliKnit elastic netting, RoastKnit, butcher coats), medical (PPE, surgical drapes, orthopedic fabrics, infant caps, lab coats), industrial (DrainKnit filtration covers, geo textiles, protective sleeves), and apparel markets (custom embroidery, freezerwear, hospitality garments). Its customer base spans national and international businesses, with a centralized Midwest location enabling quick delivery across the United States.

The company emphasizes its family-owned integrity, competitive pricing, and commitment to quality, underscored by SQF certification achieved in 2018 for food safety. Dickson differentiates itself through collaborative custom product development, emergency response capabilities, and a nationwide sales team that provides ongoing consultation.

name: DigitTron Technologies Inc
old_description: Our electronics manufacturing expertise and processes will get your products to market faster.
about:
DigitTron Technologies Inc. is an electronic manufacturing services provider headquartered in Shawnee, Kansas, a suburb of Kansas City. Founded in 2011, the company was co-founded by Victor Turnbaugh and became a subsidiary of Pivot International in 2016, gaining access to a global network with offices in the UK, Hong Kong, and manufacturing facilities in Asia.

The company operates a 13,800-square-foot humidity-controlled facility where it provides surface-mount assembly, conventional through-hole assembly, X-ray inspection, box-build integration, potting, and conformal coating. Its staff of industrial designers, engineers, technicians, and assemblers follows IPC workmanship standards and handles both prototype and full production runs.

DigitTron serves customers in telecommunications, medical devices, agriculture, transportation, lighting, and general industrial markets. Its client base includes start-ups scaling from prototype to high-volume production as well as established firms across the United States.

The firm emphasizes quality through adherence to ANSI/J-STD-001, ANSI/J-STD-002, and IPC-A-610D standards, and it leverages its parent company’s global supply chain to reduce lead times and costs while maintaining on-time delivery.

name: Dixon Power Systems
old_description: After 17 years of owning an automotive repair shop, Jon Dixon needed a new challenge and had a growing interest in Renewable Energy. With the encouragement of his wife Holly, the business was launched. Dixon Power Systems began as a part-time business in the spring of 1999 and expanded to full time in January of 2005.
about:
Dixon Power Systems operates from Lincoln, Nebraska, where Jon and Holly Dixon launched the business in the spring of 1999 after Jon spent 17 years running an automotive repair shop. The venture began part‑time and moved to full‑time operation in January 2005, driven by Jon’s growing interest in renewable energy and Holly’s encouragement.

The company designs and installs solar photovoltaic and wind generation systems for customers seeking energy independence. A storefront allows visitors to learn about and purchase equipment for producing their own electricity. Jon applies his automotive mechanical and electrical background to tailor each system for site‑specific constraints, maximizing efficiency while addressing environmental concerns and ease of operation.

Clients include homeowners and remote‑site operators who are too far from utility lines, want backup power, or wish to reduce reliance on fossil fuels. The Dixons have served customers across Nebraska and the broader Midwest through project design, installation, and ongoing technical support.

Jon’s motivation stemmed from a desire to translate his hands‑on mechanical expertise into the renewable sector, while Holly values the independence of business ownership and helping clients build systems that work. Their involvement in community education — teaching at local colleges, exhibiting at energy fairs, and serving on the Nebraskans for Solar board — reflects a commitment to growing the regional clean‑energy knowledge base.

name: Drake Plastics Ltd. Co.
old_description: The science behind Drake’s state-of-the-art injection molding operation assures exceptional quality and consistency in molded parts. When critical tolerances and other features are impractical or impossible to achieve with injection molding alone, we can deploy our precision machining capabilities to provide hybrid molded/machined part solutions to meet the specifications required.
about:
Drake Plastics Ltd. Co. is headquartered in Cypress, Texas. The company was founded in March 1996 by Steve Quance, who recognized an opportunity to supply machinable stock shapes in specialty grades of Torlon® PAI polymer after a major supplier discontinued a product needed for the Javelin missile program. Quance, then an Advanced Products Manager at a large stock shapes supplier, invested personally to establish Drake Plastics and fulfill that initial order.

Today, Drake operates what it describes as the world’s largest facility dedicated to processing ultra high-performance polymers. The company extrudes stock shapes — rod, plate, seamless tube, sheet, film, and balls — in Torlon PAI, PEEK, Ryton PPS, AvaSpire PAEK, Ultem PEI, and proprietary Drake PAI grades. It also runs injection molding and precision machining operations, enabling hybrid molded/machined parts when tolerances exceed what molding alone can achieve. Additional in-house services include re-curing, annealing, priming, coating, laser engraving, CT inspection, CMM inspection, and mechanical testing.

Drake serves aerospace, defense, oil and gas, transportation, electrical, and fluid-handling industries. Its customer base includes OEMs, government agencies (such as the Javelin missile program), universities, distributors, and fabricators worldwide. Products are shipped globally from the Cypress facility, with sales offices in Germany, France, and Taiwan providing local support.

The company emphasizes its near-net stock shapes that minimize machining waste, a quality system certified to AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015, and an on-time delivery rate typically above 98%. Its culture of product and process development aims to deliver unique solutions not available elsewhere, a philosophy rooted in the founding mission to produce what no other supplier could or would.
